root_cause.text: In the wireless extensions compat ioctl handlers, a stack-allocated `struct iw_point` on 64-bit kernels was partially initialized from `struct compat_iw_point` without zeroing its 32-bit padding hole, allowing uninitialized kernel stack data to be copied back to user space.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(&iwp, 0, sizeof(iwp));` in both `compat_standard_call()` and `compat_private_call()` and explicitly notes that `struct iw_point has a 32bit hole on 64bit arches`, showing the leak came from uninitialized padding in `iwp` used by WEXT compat ioctls.

Next we can kill the hacks in fs/compat_ioctl.c
bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the function body is sufficient: it shows the exact compat-handling path for `struct iw_point` on 64-bit kernels. The vulnerable construct is present because `struct iw_point iwp;` is stack-allocated and only partially initialized from `struct compat_iw_point` with `iwp.pointer = compat_ptr(iwp_compat->pointer);`, `iwp.length = iwp_compat->length;`, and `iwp.flags = iwp_compat->flags;`. There is no zeroing of the structure or its padding before it is passed to `ioctl_standard_iw_point(&iwp, ...)`, so the uninitialized padding-hole issue can exist. The fix is not present here because there is no `memset(&iwp, 0, sizeof(iwp))` or equivalent explicit initialization to prevent stack data leakage.
